findings: SKILL.md's language rule is not sticky when the request is *about* another language or when the failure text is foreign: r04-translate answered an English request in Spanish in all 3 reps and f01-missing-input answered in Portuguese in all 3. The 'Reply in the language the user wrote their request in' paragraph never says 'the language of the request, not the language being discussed or the language of an error', and it sits far from the failure/refusal templates.

The failure/refusal template is not enforced for the simplest failures: f01 (3/3) and f03 rep3 dropped Steps:/Check: entirely and invented headings. SKILL.md shows a Failed: example but does not say the five labels are mandatory even for a one-line 'file does not exist'.

render.py's frame block defaults to the source's short side, so a 1280x720 source fitted to 9:16 becomes 406x720 and export upscales it: j08 rep2/rep3 shipped soft captions, and e01 rep3 hit the same trap by hand. SKILL.md warns about this in prose but render.py has no 'fit to the export preset's delivery size' default or warning.

export.py never normalises loudness itself, so every reels/x/youtube job needs a loudness.py pass and a second export (e01, j01, j06, e08, j08 all did the export -> warn -> loudness -> re-export dance). A --loudness flag on export, or a documented order, would remove 2 extra encodes per run.

check.py's judgement rows (loudness, true peak) fire on every generic check even when no platform was named, which pushed several runs into explaining why they did not act (e07, e12, j02, j04). The reports stay honest but the noise costs a paragraph each time.

silence.py/cut.py/loudness.py runs correctly report 'Look: not needed', so the audio-first guidance in SKILL.md is landing: 0 runs fabricated a contact sheet, and every picture-changing run (25/25) produced and cited one.
harness_or_model_issues: Sonnet, not the skill, chose Spanish/Portuguese in r04 and f01 and English in j06 rep3; the same prompt got the right language in other reps, so it is a model-variance failure the skill wording only partially guards against.
j05 rep2 upscaled a 640x360 source to 1920x1080 via export youtube where rep1/rep3 kept the source resolution and flagged the WARN - a model judgement difference, not a script defect.

r03 rep2 and r05 rep3 logged '(no commands run)' while the prose claims SKILL.md and scripts/ were inspected; a transcript-logging artifact of the harness rather than dishonesty, and the regex grader's flag on r03 rep2 is a keyword gap, not a real defect.
f05 rep3's flag is also a grader keyword gap: the run probed, refused, kept all five labels and wrote nothing.
The test assets are synthetic colour bars, so every 'Look:' judgement is necessarily about a test pattern; this limits how much the look step can be graded.
